description: The wire calls of the Slen SDKs: which HTTP operation of the API's OpenAPI spec each public call makes, and which SDKs offer it. The key is the name of the call in every SDK and in the reference: the call as a caller writes it after the client in PHP and TypeScript (`operations.execute` is `$slen->operations()->execute(…)` and `slen.operations.execute(…)`; a method of the client itself has no dot). Python writes each segment of the key in snake_case and nothing else (`customers.topUp` is `slen.customers.top_up(…)`, `operations.executeAsync` is `slen.operations.execute_async(…)`, `health` is `slen.health()`); its help slice gives the key as the call's `name` and the Python method as its `member`, so a reader of the reference has one name for a call. `operation` is `METHOD /path` as the spec writes the path; `sdks` names the SDKs that offer the call (`php`, `python`, `typescript`) — every call is in all three. A call that repeats one operation names that operation: `executions.wait` reads the status until the run is over, `customers.listAll` and `customers.entriesAll` read page after page, each with the cursor of the page before. A public call that makes no request of the API (`webhooks.verify`, `webhooks.constructEvent`, `flush` in TypeScript, `close` in Python) has no line here: each contract test lists it in its `NOT_CALLS` with the reason. The contract tests read this file and keep no table of their own: a row of the contract test of each SDK is a line here that names its SDK, and the other way round, and each call is driven to the method and the path its line names — with no spec, and against the spec where there is one. Each help slice copies `operation` onto its calls. The rules are in the AGENTS.md of each package.
